findings.location: sections/concise/02-overview.tex, Allegorical row, clause 'The garment is charity, which the Bridegroom himself wore (Gregory; Augustine)' (physical page 1)
findings.problem: The parenthesis credits both Fathers with the whole clause, including its reason. That reason is Gregory's: the Bridegroom himself had charity when he came to the wedding at which he joined the Church to himself (Hom. in Ev. 38, 9: 'quia hanc in se conditor noster habuit, dum ad sociandae sibi Ecclesiae nuptias venit'). Augustine, in Sermo 90 (NPNF1-6, sections 5-6 and 9), makes the garment charity, puts it on 'to do honour to the Bridegroom', 'in honour of the union', and sets the Bridegroom's prayer for his enemies before the guest as the pattern. He does not say that the Bridegroom wore the garment. The study's own allegorical sense in sections/20-wedding-garment.tex and research/interpretations.md section 1.4 give this clause to Gregory alone. The component's header comment also says that each witness is named beside the clause he states and no other. This is advisory, like STU-008 and RES-010, because Augustine holds no view contrary to the clause.
findings.required_result: Cite each clause to the Father who states it. For example: 'The garment is charity (Gregory; Augustine), which the Bridegroom himself wore (Gregory), or ...'. Keep the row otherwise unchanged, so that page 1 still holds the map and exactly four sense rows.

findings.location: sections/concise/10-commentary.tex: 'The evening sacrifice', last paragraph ('At a Mass celebrated with incense the priest says the Gradual's verse again ... (Ordo Missae, no. 1037)', page 10); 'Many called, few chosen', third paragraph ('the Gradual that the priest says again over the altar at a Mass with incense ... the Secret whose words the Placeat repeats', page 10) and last paragraph ('The Mass that began with God promising to hear his people from any tribulation ends by asking to cleave to his commandments always', page 11); compare sections/concise/04-themes.tex, the Gradual paragraph (page 3) and the Offertory-Secret and Communion-Postcommunion paragraphs (page 4)
findings.problem: The commentary restates textual observations that the Themes pages already make. The priest's saying of Ps 140:2 as he incenses the altar at the Offertory appears three times (themes page 3; commentary page 10, twice). The Secret's and the Placeat's shared 'oculis tuae maiestatis' is stated in the themes and invoked again in the commentary. The themes' closing sentence, 'The Mass that began with God promising ... ends with a prayer to hold to his commandments semper', returns almost word for word as the commentary's penultimate sentence. The three-document profile asks that the page-5 commentary 'deepen and compare the earlier movement instead of repeating it', and the document is already at its 12-page ceiling. This is advisory because each repetition is short and true and none misleads.
findings.required_result: Change the commentary, not pages 3-4, whose extent is fixed. Where a reading needs an observation the Themes pages already give, refer back to it in a clause rather than restating it. For example, reduce the Ordo Missae no. 1037 sentence in 'The evening sacrifice' to the clause the third reading needs. Also rewrite the closing of 'Many called, few chosen' so that it does not repeat the themes' 'The Mass that began ...' sentence.

findings.location: sections/concise/04-themes.tex, last paragraph ('each developed at length in the expansive study with four senses of its own', page 4); sections/concise/90-apparatus.tex, 'Relation to the expansive study' (page 11); synthesis.tex and main.tex, \propertitle first field
findings.problem: The concise's body sends the reader to 'the expansive study'. That is a term from the production contract, and the reader has not been told what it names. The scope appendix identifies the companion only as 'The Nineteenth Sunday after Pentecost'. The concise prints the same title on its own page 1, because both entrypoints open with \propertitle{The Nineteenth Sunday after Pentecost}{Dominica decima nona post Pentecosten}. A reader holding the concise is therefore told that the full argument is in a work carrying the title on the page in front of him. In print, only main.tex's fourth \propertitle field distinguishes the study: 'The wedding garment, the call to the highways, and the evening sacrifice: a study of the proper in three readings'.
findings.required_result: Identify the companion so that a reader can tell it from the concise. For example, call it 'the full study' in the body. In the scope appendix, name it by its distinguishing subtitle, or by its catalogue label 'Full PDF'. Leave the extent of pages 3-4 unchanged.

observations.location: sections/concise/02-overview.tex, Allegorical row; evaluations/blocking-findings-v1.toml, RES-010 and STU-008
observations.note: This is the third finding in this run where a joint parenthesis or colon construction credits a second Father with the first Father's distinctive clause: RES-010 in interpretations.md, STU-008 in the study opening, and SYN-001 on the concise page 1. It is the missing profile or fragment criterion that the study-review observation already named. No gate can see how far a clause-level attribution reaches.

summary: Cold review of the concise study synthesis.tex (six components under sections/concise/, sealed hashes confirmed). I rebuilt it to a fixed point in scratch; the PDF is byte-identical to build/claude/.../59-nineteenth-after-pentecost-synthesis.pdf: 12 pages, no overfull or undefined-reference warnings, fonts embedded. The settled zref evidence places the inventory and the four sense rows on physical page 1, the dossier alone on page 2, Themes and Movement on pages 3-4 (both full), and the commentary from page 5. Checked evidence: I compared the text sentence by sentence with the accepted study (sections/00-80), research/interpretations.md and the generated chronology annotations. Every quotation in the concise matches the study verbatim. I spot-checked quotations and loci in the tracked witnesses: Gregory Hom. 38.1-14 (Wikisource Migne), Augustine Sermo 90.1-10 (NPNF1-6) and Enarr. 77, 104, 118, 137, 140 (NPNF1-8), Hilary In Matth. 22.3-7 (PL 9 text layer), Irenaeus IV.36.5-6 (ANF 1), Chrysostom Hom. 69 in Mt (NPNF1-10) and Hom. 14 in Eph (NPNF1-13), Rabanus (PL 107), Schuster pp. 171-174 and Bellarmine. Findings: no new source-dependent claim, the controlling claim of each of the three readings present, and the material differences kept (charity or the new man, gift or work, the burned city, the highways, the present or the heavenly feast, and the Passion or the works of mercy as the evening sacrifice). The complementary readings are compared without staged conflict. The concise follows the liturgical-commentator rule and contains no lectionary history. Its six questions carry actual comparisons; the first three follow the readings' own questions with their alternatives set side by side, and the last three set the readings against one another. Limits: I did not re-read the PL 26 page images for Jerome (the tracked record holds no payload), the Liège or Venice Aquinas, or the PG Greek; for those I relied on the verbatim agreement with the accepted study. Verdict: PASS, with three advisories on one page-1 joint attribution, restated observations, and how the companion study is named.
